title: Single-Cell ICN Neuron Mapping and 3D Heart Reconstruction with Tissue Mapper
author: Clara Leung
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.bdz5i786

steps.title: Prepare and Stain Heart Samples
steps.instruction: Prepare rat heart samples using one of two fixation and staining methods to visualize neurons.

substeps.instruction: Method 1: Anesthetize rats with 5% isoflurane, dissect hearts, and fix overnight in 4% paraformaldehyde. Perform whole-mount diffusion staining for 7 days in 0.1% Cresyl Echt Violet (0.05g in 50 mL distilled H2O and 150 µL glacial acetic acid).

Method 2: Perfuse animals through the abdominal aorta with phosphate-buffered saline at 280 mmHg until exsanguinated, then perfusion-fix with 200 mL 10% neutral buffered formalin at 280 mmHg. Dissect hearts and fix overnight in 10% neutral buffered formalin. Perform whole-mount diffusion staining in 0.1% Cresyl Echt Violet for 14 days.
Process hearts in a Sakura Tissue Tek VIP 3000 tissue processor.
Inject molten paraffin through great vessels using a syringe to fill chambers and remove air bubbles, then embed hearts in paraffin.

steps.title: Digitize and Process Images
steps.instruction: Digitize the FFPE blocks and assemble the image stack using MBF Bioscience software.

substeps.instruction: Digitize samples with a Knife Edge Scanning Microscope (KESM) to produce individual jpg tiles for each Z position.
Stitch jpg tiles into individual planes (uncompressed TIFF format).
Convert uncompressed TIFFs into JP2000 format.
Assemble JP2000 planes into a stack (.jpx) using 40:1 lossy compression.

steps.title: Initialize Tissue Mapper Software
steps.instruction: Set up the software environment and project metadata.

substeps.instruction: Install and license Tissue Mapper (version 2020.1.1) on the workstation.
Set an API key in the profile to pull the ontology list from SciCrunch.
Create a new document by entering subject information: species (Rattus Norvegicus), sample ID, sex, and age.
Specify the species and organ (Heart) to access curated SPARC anatomy terms and press 'Begin'.

steps.title: Load and Configure Image Stack
steps.instruction: Import the processed image data and verify scaling.

substeps.instruction: Open the .jpx image stack via File > Open > Image stack.
Verify or adjust XYZ scaling properties in the dialog box.
Check 'Create sections for this stack' and click 'OK' to load.

steps.title: Configure Workspace Layout
steps.instruction: Optimize the interface for efficient annotation.

substeps.instruction: Under the 'Workspace' ribbon, enable 'AutoMove'.
Dock the 'Macro view', 'Image organizer', and 'Serial Section Manager' windows.

steps.title: Perform Anatomical Contouring
steps.instruction: Trace the heart's anatomical structures across the image stack.

substeps.instruction: In the 'Trace' ribbon > 'CONTOURS' submenu, click 'Contour selection' and choose the desired SPARC anatomy term.
Set tracing options to 'Freehand'.
Navigate to a section using the 'Serial Section Manager' and zoom in.
Draw the contour by clicking to place points or by right-clicking and selecting 'Continuous tracing' (recommended for digital tablets).
Right-click and select 'Close contour' or 'End open contour' to finish.
Move to different sections using PgUp or PgDn keys and repeat the process.
Use the 'Show current section' button in the Serial Section Manager to hide contours from other sections.
For stacks > 1000 sections, contour structures (atria, ventricles, and major blood vessels) in intervals of 10-20 sections until complete.

steps.title: Map ICN Neurons
steps.instruction: Identify and mark neurons of the intrinsic cardiac nervous system (ICN).

substeps.instruction: In the Markers toolbar, select a circle marker, right-click to rename it 'ICN', and change the color to yellow.
Enable 'Show Marker Summary' and 'Show Marker Names' in the Markers Toolbar.
Navigate to sections and place markers on neurons where the nucleus is most prominent, marking every 4th section to avoid double-counting.

steps.title: Visualize 3D Reconstruction
steps.instruction: Generate and interact with the 3D model of the heart and neurons.

substeps.instruction: To visualize contours and markers only: Deselect 'Show current section' in the Serial Section Manager, then in the 'Image Organizer' under the 'Images' ribbon, deselect the eye (or press 'Toggle Checked Visibility') to hide image data.
To visualize contours, markers, and image data: Ensure the eye is checked in the 'Image Organizer' to show image data.
Press the '3D Visualize' button under the 'Trace' or 'Workspace' ribbon to open the 3D viewer.
Interact with the model to show/hide/edit contours and markers, create video clips, export representations, or reslice the volume in XY, XZ, and YZ planes.

steps.title: Save Project Data
steps.instruction: Export the annotation and mapping data for future use.

substeps.instruction: Go to the 'File' ribbon, select 'Save as', and choose 'Data File' to save as an XML document (.xml).
